content.value_statement: US state privacy requirements create difficult applicability, disclosure, and request-handling decisions. This public guide frames AI-assisted compliance planning, with legal verification and implementation handled separately.
actual_capabilities: Provides topic guidance for AI-assisted state privacy applicability reviews using business context.
Identifies state-specific privacy disclosure topics, including California, Texas, and Maryland.
Outlines DSR planning topics covering intake, verification, access, deletion, and appeals.
Highlights Global Privacy Control and targeted advertising opt-out considerations.
Introduces California Delete Act and data broker registration review topics.
limitations: Only SKILL.md is included; the advertised logic engine, scripts, extension source, and templates are absent.
No bundled legal sources, verified threshold dataset, or live calendar substantiate the advertised 2026 accuracy and updates through 2028.
The guide excludes federal HIPAA and GLBA filings and employee or B2B data contexts outside California.
Outputs require independent legal review and do not implement policies, register businesses, or process requests automatically.

use_cases.title: Prepare an applicability review
use_cases.description: Organize customer counts, revenue information, and advertising practices into questions for a state privacy applicability review.

use_cases.title: Plan policy disclosures
use_cases.description: Develop a preliminary disclosure outline and identify state-specific issues for counsel to verify before publication.

use_cases.title: Design request handling
use_cases.description: Draft an intake, verification, routing, and escalation plan for consumer privacy requests.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the review scope
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this guide, summarize the privacy review topics for a US online retailer. Separate included guidance from unavailable automation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: understand the guide before using it for planning.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an applicability checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare an applicability checklist for [states] using [customer counts], [revenue], and [data practices]. Mark missing facts and require current authoritative sources for thresholds.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: collect business facts for legal review.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a disclosure outline
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a privacy notice outline for [business] in [states], based on [data practices]. Flag state-specific provisions and unresolved legal questions. Do not assume compliance.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: prepare a policy outline for counsel.

prompt_templates.title: Design a request workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a DSR workflow for [business] in [states], covering verification, access, deletion, appeals, and GPC. Label unverified deadlines and implementation dependencies; use synthetic examples.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: plan coordinated privacy operations without claiming automated deployment.

output_examples.input: Our retailer serves Connecticut and Virginia and uses advertising pixels. What should we collect before reviewing applicability?
output: Collect resident counts by state, measurement periods, revenue details, and relevant exemptions.
Document pixel data flows, advertising purposes, recipients, and contractual restrictions.
Verify current statutory thresholds and effective dates before reaching an applicability conclusion.

output_examples.input: Outline a deletion request workflow for our support team.
output: Intake: record the request date, jurisdiction, request type, and assigned owner.
Verification: use proportionate identity checks and restrict access to request records.
Review: confirm applicable deadlines, exemptions, and any appeal obligations with counsel.
Fulfillment: coordinate approved deletion actions and document the response.
Escalation: route disputed requests and exceptions to the privacy team.

best_practices: Verify every threshold, exemption, deadline, and effective date against current official sources before relying on an output.
Provide aggregate business facts and synthetic request examples instead of identifiable customer records.
Require counsel to review applicability decisions and policy language before publication or operational use.
anti_patterns: Treating this public guide as an installed compliance engine or automatic legal update service.
Applying example thresholds or response windows universally without checking state law and business facts.
Assuming generated text implements GPC handling, submits registrations, or fulfills consumer requests.

faq.question: What is included in this package?
faq.answer: The package contains one public SKILL.md guide. Scripts, extension source, templates, and an executable compliance engine are not included.

faq.question: Does it verify current state privacy thresholds?
faq.answer: The guide claims verified 2026 thresholds, but includes no supporting dataset or legal citations. Confirm current requirements using authoritative sources.

faq.question: Can it automatically process data subject requests?
faq.answer: No request-processing integration is included. The guide can inform AI-assisted workflow drafts, but implementation and operation require separate tools and review.

faq.question: Which topics are outside its stated scope?
faq.answer: The guide excludes federal HIPAA and GLBA filings. It limits employee and B2B data coverage to California.

faq.question: Does it provide live updates through 2028?
faq.answer: The guide advertises a live calendar, but no calendar service or update mechanism is included in the reviewed package.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: The marketplace lists these tools as supported. They can use the guide as context; legal verification and software integrations remain separate responsibilities.
